INTERNSHIP INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
NAME
BRANCH
SOHAM GHADGE
ELECTRONICS & TELECOMMUNICATION
Eligibility Criteria
CGPA: 6.5
Eligible Branches: CS, IT and Circuit 
branches
Active Backlogs: No
Dead Backlogs: Yes
Stipend: INR 75,000 per month
Role: Institutional Clients Group (ICG Tech) 
The entire process was divided in the following rounds:
Online Test Round ( 1hr 30 minutes)
Interview Rounds:
       1) Technical Round ( 50minutes )
       2) HR Round ( 15 minutes )

PRE-PLACEMENT TALK
This is the time where you understand about the company, its
 goals, its objectives and their work areas. It is a great time for yo
u t o as k an y question s yo u hav e abou t th e role , th e proces s a
nd anythi ng y ou ha ve in mi nd relat ed to t he upcomi ng interns
hip process. It might seem like a waste of time to a few but it’s not. You can use the company’s language and values in your answers which could give you an upper hand in the interview process. .
Duration : 1 hour
ONLINE ASSESSMENT
Duration : 1 hr 30 minutes
The online assessment for each roles were different. Since I had
 ICG Tech role as my 1st preference, I had the following format - 
Coding Section (45 minutes - 2 questions)
SQL ( 15 minutes - 12 MCQs)
React ( 15 minutes - 12 MCQs)
Angular ( 15 minutes - 12 MCQs)
Coding Section -
I didn't expect this section to go so smoothly, as I received
 questions from the previous year, which I had luckily practice
d beforehand . Thi s preparatio n gav e m e a n advantage . It' s wor
th mentioning that learning from your seniors' interview experien
ces can be invaluab le, so ple ase t ake the t ime to go thro ugh t
hem. The questions asked to me were as follows - 
Question 1: A stock trader deals in N stocks and calculates
 their relative price changes. The trader's lucky number is K, s
o they want to invest in the stock with the Kth smallest relati
ve price. Write an algorithm to find the Kth smallest stock price 
from the list of N stocks.
Solution Logic: Sort the list of stock prices in ascending order
 and return the Kth smallest value by accessing the (K-1) index 
in the sorted list.

This section included 12 multiple-choice questions on SQL, with
 topics ranging from basic queries to DDL, DML, TCL commands
, and aggregate functions. SQL being my strongest domain, I found 
this section very manageable.
SQL -
Question: You are given N flowers and their stem 
        lengths. Arrange the first K flowers in increasing order 
        of stem length, and the remaining (N-K) flowers in decreasing order.
Solution Logic: Sort the first K flowers in ascending order and the
 remaining (N-K) flowers in descending order. Use the sort functio
n twice, with the second sort using a comparator (greater<int>()) for 
descending order.
React -
This section included 12 multiple-choice questions on React,
 focusing on key concepts such as React lifecycle methods, type
s o f components , an d cod e snippet s wit h missin g terms . This 
section was of medium difficulty.
Angular - 
I wasn't fully prepared for this section, but after reading about it
 in my senior's interview experiences, I decided to prepare for i
t the day before the OA. The section ranged from medium to ha
rd difficult y. F or t he questio ns I wasn 't su re abou t, I selected 
random options since there was no negative marking.
INTERVIEW
The interview was scheduled online on October 4th and
 conducted via Zoom. Out of 200 registered participants, only 4
0 students were shortlisted for interviews—28 for the ICG role a
nd 12 for the PBWM role. My interview was set for 11:30 AM but 
was delayed by an hour. For the ICG tech role, there were only two 
rounds: one technical and one HR.

I joined the interview at 12:30 PM sharp and started with a warm
 greeting. The interviewer kicked off by asking me to introduc
e myself. This is a typical question, and it's important to prepare f
or it in advance. I made sure my introduction was impactful, steering 
the conversation toward databases, which is my strongest area.
Databases: I was asked to compare NoSQL (MongoDB) and SQL
 databases. I explained their differences in depth, I also mentione
d about  horizontal and vertical scaling which led to another de
ep discussion about the scaling methods! This helped me to ge
t a strong start with the interview! Then he asked me why I o
ften choose MongoDB for my projects, to which I emphasized o
n its flexibility and performance with complex queries. The inter
viewer also asked about the concept of a document in MongoDB 
and how it contrasts with a row in SQL, and I explained the structural 
differences.
DSA : Next, I faced a problem involving an n x n x n 3D array. The
 task was to find occurrences of a specific word or string within th
e array. I started with a brute-force solution. He then asked me 
to optimise it to which I asked for a hint. However, the intervie
wer realized the question wasn’t framed correctly and shifted focu
s to Git, where I admitted I wasn’t as confident. He appreciated the 
honesty and moved on.
Web Dev : He asked with about which frontend and backend
 technologies I had worked in, to which I replied MERN Stack! H
e then asked me where majorly I had contributed in the project. I to
ld him that I was majorly involved in the backend side of it like 
JWT Auth and Database management. We then entered to discuss a
bout JWT auth process in depth and what all error codes we face d
uring authentication. I was asked about the common error code
s that might arise during authentication processes, particular
ly: 401 (Unauthorized), 402 (Payment Required), 403 (Forbidden), 
404 (Not Found) and 501 (Internal Server Error). I was surprised a
s I didnt expect this to be asked although I was familiar with 401 
and 404, I told him that I didnt know about 402, 403 and 501. He then told me 
about 501 !
TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes)

Additionally, I was asked to give a wild guess about the difference
between 401 and 501 , where I clarified that 401 indicates an
authentication failure, while 501 refers to the server's inability to
recognize the request method. Boom this is how I ended up with
Web Dev! That was a good grilling session!
Computer Networks (CCN) : The interviewer tested my knowledge
of computer networks since I belong to EXTC, particularly in the
context of the Application Layer protocol. He wanted me to explain
the differences between HTTP and HTTPS. I explained that HTTPS
adds a layer of encryption (via SSL/TLS), making it more secure
compared to HTTP, which transmits data in plaintext. Luckily I had
this in my sem at the moment and had given a MST on it , indeed I
answered this very well!
Conclusion :
At the end, the interviewer asked if I had any questions for him. I
used this opportunity to ask about his career journey and his
current role in the company. This led to a meaningful 6-7 minute
conversation, which gave me deeper insight into his experience and
the company’s work culture.
Key Takeaways
Throughout the interview, I stayed confident in the areas I was
strong in, like databases and web dev. When asked about Git, I was
upfront about my lack of confidence, and that honesty was
appreciated. It’s crucial not to bluff—if you don’t know something,
just say so. This builds trust and reflects well on your integrity.
My interview concluded at 12:55 PM, after which I had lunch while
anxiously waiting for the results. By 1:45 PM, the results were out,
and thankfully, I was selected for the next round—the HR round.
Out of all the candidates, only 9 students were shortlisted for this
round for my role. 
I felt confident heading into the HR round, knowing that my strong
communication skills and ability to connect with people would
serve me well.

TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes)
HR ROUND (15 minutes)
My HR round was scheduled for 2:45 PM, and it followed the usual
 format of HR interviews. I was asked to introduce myself, tal
k about my hobbies, family background, and whether I’d be open 
to relocating to Pune. The interviewer also inquired about my future 
plans and why I chose Citi as my potential employer.
The conversation then shifted to Citi's three leadership
 principles. I was asked how I align with them, to which I provide
d examples from my experience managing Ecell’s flagship event, 
UNICUS, demonstrating leadership and organizational skills.
The interviewer also covered a few standard questions like
 whether I knew anyone already working at Citi or if I had an
y connections with government employees. I made sure to end t
he interview on a strong note with a closing statement, reaffirm
ing my interest in the role, and asked a few thoughtful questions 
about Citi and its work culture.
Conclusion -  At around 8.30, we got the result and about 10
 people were selected for the internship (7 for ICG role and 3 fo
r PBWM role) and I was proud to be one of them!

TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes)
Preparation Tips
1.Choose a DSA Sheet: Follow any DSA sheet that suits you—
Striver, Arsh Goyal, Love Babbar, or Neetcode 75. I personally
 found Striver Sheet better. Focus on understanding the concepts
, no matter where you practice from. 
Striver_SDE_Sheet
2. Fundamentals: For core subjects like OS, DBMS, and CN, any
 YouTube playlist will work. If you've studied them well in your 
course, a quick revision a day before the interview will suffice.
3. Be Ready for Common Questions: Frame your responses to
 basic questions like "Tell me about yourself," "What are you
r strengths and weaknesses," and "Where do you see yourself 
in the next few years?" Answer confidently, and use the STAR 
method for situation-based questions.
4. Study Interview Experiences: Read as many interview
 experiences as you can—GFG, Glassdoor, this drive,etc. Sometimes, you might encounter the same questions in your own interview, boosting your confidence .
5. Know Your Resume: Be well-versed with the projects listed on
 your resume. Whether it was a team effort or individual work, yo
u should be able to explain the flow and rationale behind your 
choices confidently.
6. Stay Resilient: Interviewing can be stressful, and rejections can
 affect your confidence. However, every failed interview is a ste
p closer to success. Learn from each experience, and remember 
that factors like luck also play a role.
7. Be Honest and Authentic: Don’t embellish your resume or bluff
 your way through questions. Interviewers can tell when you’re 
being dishonest, so always speak about what you know.
8. Get Support: Talk to trusted seniors or friends. They can offer
 guidance, share experiences, and help you navigate the process. You're not alone in this journey .
9. Practice Your Introduction: Practicing how you introduce
 yourself is important, especially to avoid forgetting key details. Try rehearsing in front of a mirror to build confidence .

TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes)
10. Research the Company: Learn about the company’s mission,
culture, and principles before your interview. Always have
thoughtful questions ready to ask the interviewer, as it shows
genuine interest.
Remember to stay calm, trust the process, and give it your all!
Good luck! :)
